note: The specs the browser and native are compared on. web/serve.py computes the native answer for each of these at start-up and writes web/expected.json; web/check.html runs the same specs in the worker and compares. Keeping them in a data file rather than in either program is what makes the two sides provably the same question.

specs.title: Wright-Fisher — neutral fixation probability
specs.claim: P(A fixes) = p0 exactly, because the frequency is a bounded martingale. This is the one carrying a real PASS: a predicted number, a measured mean, and a tolerance of z standard errors.

specs.title: Repressilator — the refusal
specs.claim: No analytic_predictions: the deterministic limit is a limit cycle, so there is no scalar for an ensemble mean to match. Native validate() raises; the browser must refuse for the same reason. A pass mark quoting a tolerance would be meaningless here, and matching the refusal is the whole verdict.

responsiveness.note: Identical work on the main thread and in the worker, measured with the MessageChannel instrument. The main-thread arm is the same-session baseline the plan requires; re-running the old slice across sessions would compare timings on a machine that swings 4x inside one session.
